parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for local .mjs ESM files, manual argv behavior, a no-external-dependency PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 implementation, two printed 16-byte hex outputs, and executable-based black-box probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated algorithm and CLI probing to two children while also doing the same probing, implementation, integration, and final delivery itself; output-file ownership was not isolated.
parallel.implementation: The parent and children each wrote overlapping PBKDF2, HMAC/SHA1, byte, CLI, and entrypoint modules. The final hierarchy used lib/bytes.mjs, lib/hash, lib/pbkdf2, lib/cli, and test6.mjs after cleanup.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent detected unexpected duplicate implementations in /output, chose one hierarchy, deleted competing files, kept a final /output/test6.mjs, and reported the resulting files as the deliverable.
parallel.verification: The run compared outputs against the executable on provided samples, Unicode inputs, repeated args, missing args, negative-looking values, help cases, and -- handling before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Both children were interrupted before final handoff. The official evaluator completed and failed the final artifact at 22/70, so local verification did not cover the failing hidden behavior.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same prompt requirements: pure local Node.js ESM modules, exact manual CLI parsing, handwritten PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior, no external dependencies, and executable probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent owned executable probing, implementation, parser patching, verification, and final delivery in one control flow without subagent delegation or shared-output ownership ambiguity.
serial.implementation: It built lib/utils/bytes.mjs, lib/crypto/sha1.mjs, lib/crypto/hmac-sha1.mjs, lib/crypto/pbkdf2.mjs, lib/cli/test6-args.mjs, and test6.mjs, then patched parser edge cases.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run added and modified one coherent hierarchy directly under /output and delivered that hierarchy without competing concurrently written files.
serial.verification: It tested executable behavior, matched samples, covered parser errors and help variants, patched explicit help-argument cases, and compared Unicode inputs before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed and failed the final serial artifact at 22/70, so the remaining defect was not exposed by the sampled local verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three rollouts, 112 LLM requests, 185 tool calls, and 408.09 agent seconds, then closed after interrupting children and cleaning shared output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout, 38 LLM requests, 83 tool calls, and 321.161 agent seconds, then closed without timeout or subagent cleanup.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: the current completed status evaluations mark both parallel and serial as solution_passed false with 22 of 70 samples passed. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel had child-created duplicate output files and a cleanup/reconciliation episode, while serial produced one hierarchy directly. That adverse parallel coordination did not produce a different official outcome here, and the shared 22/70 failure is best treated as an ordinary uncovered implementation or evaluator-hidden behavior gap rather than a proven concurrency-caused failure.
parallel_contributors: Parallel spawned two child agents that wrote overlapping /output files while the parent also implemented and tested.
The parent later saw unexpected duplicate implementations and deleted/reconciled output files before final delivery.
serial_contributors: Serial kept probing, implementation, parser patching, and verification in one control flow.
Serial delivered one coherent hierarchy but still failed the same official hidden suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs locally matched samples and selected CLI edge cases, yet both official evaluations failed 48 of 70 cases; the raw evidence does not expose the hidden failing inputs.
No discordant official outcome is present, so the parallel write pattern is not claimed as the sole or necessary cause of the score.
evaluator_effects: The completed official evaluator is the source of truth for both outcomes and records identical pass counts.
